When cybersecurity research firm Calif published details Tuesday of a potentially major Java security flaw, dubbed Java4Shell, it described an unauthenticated attacker’s ability to read Java heap memory, steal private keys, tokens, and session secrets, and reach remote code execution (RCE).

description:
Attackers briefly hijacked Microsoft’s official Agent Framework package on PyPI and used it to distribute credential-stealing malware capable of harvesting cloud tokens, developer secrets and CI/CD credentials from developer workstations and automated build systems, according to multiple security researchers.

Two malicious versions of the package, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, appeared on PyPI on November 17 and stayed live for less than an hour.

title: Attackers hijack Microsoft’s agent-framework package to steal Azure and CI credentials

description:
Microsoft has launched a pair of AI coding models that it says can compete with offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic, marking its latest effort to build proprietary AI capabilities and reduce reliance on the partners that helped fuel its generative AI push.

The two new models, MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash, were launched at Ignite 2026. MAI Code 2 is designed for common enterprise coding tasks such as deep debugging, implementing changes across multiple files, repository-wide reasoning, and user interface development. title: Microsoft launches MAI Code 2 models to challenge OpenAI and Anthropic in AI coding

description:
I was talking with my daughter the other day. We made a bet five years ago that I lost. I bet her that by this week non-fungible tokens (NFTs) would be a major part of gaming. I was obviously wrong. She made the point that I don’t know anything about the gaming community, and she’s clearly right about that. 

She did admit that I was right about one thing — that agentic coding would become the norm. (I wish I had bet her about that instead, but I didn’t see that coming at all five years ago…) Like many young people, she was skeptical about AI in general, and didn’t like the idea of using it to write code.
